name: arguing over political symbols
old_label: arguing over a political symbol on the canvas
gloss: Members argue over a political or religious symbol on the canvas: what it means, whether it belongs, whether to take it down.
must_show: A symbol argued over for its politics: the hammer and sickle as a sign of occupation, Deus Vult as an alt-right sign, a religious symbol judged too divisive, MH17 drawn on a flag, partisan marks on a shared flag.
must_not_show: National emblems added with no argument (T3-113); covering hate symbols (T3-146); ideology argued in general from the canvas (T3-179).
decide_when_both: A symbol argued over and then covered: T3-080 when the argument leads, T3-146 when it is a hate symbol and the covering leads.

discriminators.question: Is a national emblem added (T3-113), or a political symbol's meaning argued (T3-080)?
Is a hate symbol covered (T3-146), or a symbol's politics argued (T3-080)?
Is one symbol on the canvas argued over (T3-080), or an ideology argued from the canvas as a whole (T3-179)?
Is one symbol's meaning argued (T3-080), or national politics read into the canvas at large (T3-130)?

varies: From Czechs calling the hammer and sickle a symbol of occupation to a Mexican room keeping religion off its mural.
two_or_half: It could be half of T3-179, politics argued from the canvas; kept apart because a particular symbol on the canvas is the object.

exemplars.quote: The Hammer and Sickle is a symbol of murder, totality and occupation for many Czechs. Let's take it down.
Det dekker flagget. Det er også symbol for alt-right bevegelsen, som /r/norge bør distansere seg fra.
Muy polarizante, se sugerio en Discord. Religion solo puede escalar conflictos lamentablemente.

name: casting fights as national history
old_label: casting canvas fights as historic national wars
gloss: Members cast canvas fights as their nations' historic wars: invasions repeated, old battles and songs replayed, occupation recalled.
must_show: A canvas fight told in the terms of a nation's real history of war or occupation: 'Russia is invading us again', a war song turned on black pixels, a takeover called a blitzkrieg reenactment, Kosovo again.
must_not_show: War language for fights between game fandoms or teams with no national history (T3-050, T3-005); national politics read into the canvas outside a fight (T3-130).
decide_when_both: A fight fought and told as history: T3-005 or T3-006 for the fighting, T3-081 added when the historical framing has concepts of its own.

discriminators.question: Is the defence told as a fight (T3-005), or cast as a nation's historic war (T3-081)?
Are taunts traded as sport (T3-050), or the fight cast in a nation's war history (T3-081)?
Is the fight told as historic war (T3-081), or national politics read into the canvas (T3-130)?

varies: From one line about an invasion again to running war narration with operations and battle names; Kosovo, Stalingrad, the Piave, blitzkrieg.
is_not: A streamer's fans calling a raid on a rival logo a war: a game-fandom war has no national history.
two_or_half: It could be half of T3-050, banter between rivals; kept apart because a nation's real history is invoked, which J asked to keep plain.

exemplars.quote: Russia is invading us again!
Il Piave mormorò "Non passa il pixel nero!".
I'm more impressed with the blitzkrieg reenactment there, taking over the French flag

name: carrying in the sub's quarrel
old_label: carrying the community's own quarrel onto the canvas
gloss: A community's own quarrel or rivalry is carried onto the canvas: one faction's slogan pushed over the other's, the rivalry fought in pixels.
must_show: A dispute or rivalry from the community's own life fought or argued on the canvas: a faction's mark pushed over another's, the rivalry declared to have reached r/place, members arguing whether outsiders will care.
must_not_show: Taunts traded with a rival community (T3-050); ideology argued (T3-179).
decide_when_both: A rivalry carried in and taunted: T3-050 when the taunts lead, T3-086 when the quarrel's marks do.

discriminators.question: Are taunts traded (T3-050), or the community's own quarrel fought in marks (T3-086)?
Is a general ideology argued (T3-179), or the community's own dispute carried onto the canvas (T3-086)?
Is a rival's work defaced (T3-006), or the community's own quarrel carried into the marks (T3-086)?

varies: From the Bitcoin block-size split to old-school and current RuneScape players and college rivalries.
two_or_half: It could be half of T3-050; kept apart because the quarrel belongs to the community's own life before the canvas.

exemplars.quote: Sorry, just pushing over the SegWit Sandcastle to build Fort Unlimited.
The rivalry has invaded r/place!
No one outside r/bitcoin and r/btc will know what segwit is, or care even if they googled it.

name: reading national politics in pixels
old_label: reading national politics into the canvas
gloss: Members read their nation's politics into the canvas: referendums, elections, governments, migration, old regimes.
must_show: National politics brought to the canvas work: the pixel fight felt as a referendum campaign, a government disowned, elections and regimes joked about, a national choice of targets.
must_not_show: One political symbol argued over (T3-080); fights cast as historic wars (T3-081).
decide_when_both: A target chosen for national political reasons and converted, as when a national room puts its own flag over another nation's: T3-068 for the converting, T3-130 for the national reason when it has concepts of its own.

discriminators.question: Is one symbol's meaning argued (T3-080), or national politics read into the canvas (T3-130)?
Is the fight cast as historic war (T3-081), or current national politics read into it (T3-130)?
Is national belonging felt (T3-145), or national politics argued (T3-130)?

varies: From Quebec's referendums to a Serbian election silence; a US member disowning the government while defending the flag.
is_not: Arguing whether the hammer and sickle should be taken down (T3-080).
two_or_half: It could be half of T3-081 or T3-080; kept apart because present-day national politics, not history or one symbol, is read in.

exemplars.quote: Je sais pas pourquoi mais j'ai été investi là dedans comme si c'était une campagne référendaire.
Just because I was born in the US doesn't mean I agree with or approve of the current administration.
This started in a small fun game of pixel art but ended being a literal political war.

name: making ethnic jokes about rivals
gloss: Members mock rival nations or peoples with ethnic jokes and slurs during the canvas fights.
must_show: Jokes, insults or slurs aimed at a rival people or nation: refugees, 'elf scum', a whole people cursed, national stereotypes used as abuse.
must_not_show: Taunts aimed at a rival community with no ethnic content (T3-050); arguing whether a taunt goes too far (T3-143).
decide_when_both: Taunts with some ethnic jokes: T3-050 when the taunting leads, T3-142 added when the ethnic jokes have concepts of their own.

discriminators.question: Is the rival a community taunted as such (T3-050), or a people or nation mocked (T3-142)?
Is the joke made (T3-142), or argued as going too far (T3-143)?
Is bigotry voiced (T3-142), or shut down (T3-182)?

varies: From mock fantasy-race insults to visitors called refugees with an ableist slur; a whole people cursed for ruining everything.
is_not: A sports sub taunting a rival team's fans (T3-050).
two_or_half: It is half of T3-050 in form; kept apart because the target is a people, which J asked to name plainly.

exemplars.quote: All these Estonian refugees getting boners because they beat us LUL
Fuck swedes. Always ruining everything.
Indonesians are elf scum confirmed

name: covering swastikas and hate symbols
gloss: Members cover swastikas, Nazi flags and other hate symbols or slurs placed on or near their work, or call others to.
must_show: Hate symbols or slurs on the canvas covered or reported: swastikas, Nazi flags, Hitler drawings, slur banners; calls for help against them; promises to cover them for others.
must_not_show: Calls to draw swastikas (T3-177); ordinary repair of stray pixels (T3-021).
decide_when_both: Hate symbols and slurs covered are T3-146; obscene drawings and ordinary insults covered are repair (T3-021). A theme that covers swastikas and refuses requests to draw them keeps T3-146 primary, with T3-177 added when the calls have concepts of their own.

discriminators.question: Are swastikas called for (T3-177), or covered (T3-146)?
Is a hate symbol or slur covered (T3-146), or the work repaired of other damage, obscene drawings included (T3-021)?
Is a hate symbol covered (T3-146), or a political symbol's meaning argued (T3-080)?

varies: From one member removing a swastika beside a flag to a leftist room promising to cover swastikas on another nation's flag.
is_not: Members turning a rival's logo into a swastika (T3-177).
two_or_half: It could be half of T3-021, repair; kept apart because hate symbols carry a meaning rooms answered as such.

exemplars.quote: Trolls are trying to write swastikas on your flag on /r/places. We at farleftside have got you covered don't worry.
/r/Eagles - We need your help with this Nazi Flag [/r/place]
Es gibt buchstäblich dünne Versuche ein Hakenkreuz neben die deutsche Flagge zu basteln

name: arguing the nation's historical record
old_label: arguing over the nation's historical record
gloss: Members argue whether their nation has always been on the right side of history.
must_show: Argument over the nation's historical record set off by the canvas: claims of always being right, massacres cited against them.
must_not_show: Fights cast as historic wars (T3-081); friendship with a historic enemy debated (T3-165).
decide_when_both: The record argued while debating a heart with an old enemy: T3-165 when the friendship leads, T3-166 when the record does.

discriminators.question: Is a canvas fight cast as historic war (T3-081), or the nation's whole record argued (T3-166)?
Is friendship with one historic enemy debated (T3-165), or the nation's own record (T3-166)?

is_not: Casting a border fight as a repeat of an old war (T3-081).
two_or_half: It is one room's kind and could be half of T3-130; kept apart because history, not present politics, is argued.

exemplars.quote: Greeks have always been on the right side of history
Εxcept for the massacres
Nah Greeks were pretty much always on the right side of history

name: calling to draw swastikas
gloss: Members call for, or take part in, drawing swastikas and Nazi imagery on the canvas, the room's own logo included.
must_show: Calls or admissions to draw swastikas or Nazi images: turning a logo into a swastika, helping change a logo into one, proposing Hitler's face.
must_not_show: Covering hate symbols (T3-146); arguing over a political symbol's meaning (T3-080).

discriminators.question: Are swastikas called for or drawn (T3-177), or covered (T3-146)?
Is the griefing for fun with no hate symbol (T3-192), or a swastika called for (T3-177)?
Is a rival's work defaced (T3-006), or a swastika drawn (T3-177)?

varies: From a proposal to turn a rival channel's logo into a swastika to members drawing one on their own room's logo.
is_not: A room painting over a swastika (T3-146).
two_or_half: It could be half of T3-006 or T3-192; kept apart because the hate symbol is the point, as J asked to name plainly.

exemplars.quote: Let's make the logo on r/place a swastika
Anyone want to turn the FH logo into an actual swastika?
i was helping changing it to a swastika a few hours ago

name: arguing ideology from the canvas
gloss: Members argue political ideology from the canvas: socialism, capitalism, anarchism, consensus, read into how the canvas was made.
must_show: Ideology argued with the canvas as evidence or occasion: r/place called decentralised socialism, capitalists said to destroy rather than build, left unity questioned, leaderless consensus praised.
must_not_show: One political symbol argued over (T3-080); a faction's own canvas doctrine (T3-190); the fairness of scripts (T3-027).
decide_when_both: A symbol argued in ideological terms: T3-080 when the symbol is the object, T3-179 when the ideology is.

discriminators.question: Is one symbol on the canvas argued (T3-080), or an ideology argued from the canvas (T3-179)?
Is a canvas faction's doctrine split (T3-190), or a political ideology argued (T3-179)?
Is the fairness of scripts argued (T3-027), or political ideology (T3-179)?

varies: From anarcho-capitalists conceding the canvas looks like socialism to leftists arguing Kronstadt.
is_not: Czechs arguing that the hammer and sickle should come down (T3-080).
two_or_half: See T3-080: politics argued from the canvas, kept two by the object.

exemplars.quote: So r/place is basically decentralize socialism.
Yeah but what do you think about Kronstadt
Typical capitalist, destroys others instead of building your own.

name: shutting down bigotry in chat
gloss: Members or moderators shut down bigoted speech in the room's thread or chat: slurs removed, a speaker shut down, racist claims answered.
must_show: Bigotry in the room's talk answered: anti-trans speech shut down in the Discord, a post removed for a slur, racist claims rebutted.
must_not_show: Hate symbols on the canvas covered (T3-146); members excluded for damage to the work (T3-121).
decide_when_both: A member banned for bigoted talk: T3-182 when the bigotry leads, T3-121 when the exclusion does.

discriminators.question: Is a hate symbol on the canvas covered (T3-146), or bigoted talk shut down (T3-182)?
Is a member excluded for damage to the work or room (T3-121), or bigoted speech shut down (T3-182)?
Is bigotry voiced (T3-142), or shut down (T3-182)?

varies: From a moderator removing a post for a slur to members shutting down an anti-trans speaker in the room's chat.
is_not: Painting over a swastika on the canvas (T3-146).
two_or_half: It could be half of T3-121 or T3-063; kept apart because bigotry, not damage or post rules, is answered.
